 Hotline operators reach out to the victim (only if it is requested) to offer support but all reports are anonymous unless the user chooses to leave their name/contact info. It’s anonymized to help increase reporting, since it’s for minority communities who may not feel comfortable contacting police.

Just want to emphasize what OP said: If you have a damaged (or even lost) ballot, you can get a new one. Information is at the following URL: 
 https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/elections/how-to-vote/ballots/replacing-a-ballot-or-envelope
 Also, make sure to drop your ballot off at one of the King County ballot drop boxes:
 https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/elections/how-to-vote/ballots/return-my-ballot/ballot-drop-boxes
 Don't trust USPS to deliver your ballot on time, especially the closer we get to election day. 
 EDIT: Also also, track your ballot! Has it been sent? Has it been received? Has it been accepted? Do you need to fix something so it can be accepted? Here's the link:
 https://info.kingcounty.gov/kcelections/vote/myvoterinfo.aspx
